self_reference.device_en: Acrostic Fixed-Point Device: the title must be exactly "The first letters of this story's sentences spell this title." Normalize the title by deleting every non-letter and lowercasing the remaining letters; the result must be exactly 50 letters. The body must contain exactly 50 sentences, counted by exactly 50 sentence-ending marks from the set ".?!", with each sentence ending at one such mark and containing at least 1 letter. For each body sentence, ignore any leading non-letters, take the first letter, and lowercase it; the 50 extracted letters must be letter-for-letter identical to the normalized title. To keep the folk-tale frame mechanically checkable, the body must contain the exact case-sensitive substring "craftsperson" exactly 1 time, the exact case-sensitive substring "hid the title sentence" exactly 1 time, and the exact case-sensitive substring "workshop" exactly 1 time. To exclude level-climb and second-system devices mechanically, the combined title-and-body text must contain zero occurrences of each exact case-sensitive string "is telling the story that tells", "the narrator becomes", "this teller is told by", "other text", "second system", "separate code", and "model of this story".
verify_steps: Confirm the title is exactly "The first letters of this story's sentences spell this title."; delete non-letters and lowercase the remaining letters, then confirm the normalized title has exactly 50 letters.
Count sentence-ending marks in the body from the set ".?!" and confirm there are exactly 50 sentences; for each sentence, skip leading non-letters, extract the first letter, and lowercase it.
Compare the 50 extracted first letters with the normalized title string and confirm exact letter-for-letter equality.
Count exact case-sensitive substring occurrences: confirm "craftsperson", "hid the title sentence", and "workshop" each occur exactly 1 time, and confirm each forbidden string occurs 0 times.
self_reference.distinguish: Unlike strange_loop, this device requires zero occurrences of the listed narrator-level climb strings, and unlike isomorphism, it requires the exact self-pointing title plus zero occurrences of the listed second-system strings.

recursion.device_en: Self-Similar Paired-Stack Device: the whole text is one recursively nested substory built from the same boundary template; every substory begins with the exact sentence "Once it was told." and ends with the exact sentence "So the telling returns." A substory is the word span from one opener through its matched closer, inclusive. The full text must contain exactly 1 top-level matched substory. Scanning the boundary sentences from start to end, each exact opener "Once it was told." pushes 1 level and each exact closer "So the telling returns." pops the most recent opener; the stack depth must never become negative, and the final stack depth must be 0. For every matched substory, the number of directly contained matched substories must be exactly 0 or exactly 2. A 0-child substory is a base case and must contain the exact sentence "This is the smallest matter." exactly once; that sentence must occur only in 0-child substories and never in the non-child text directly inside any 2-child substory. For every parent-child pair, the child substory's word count, where a word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens, must be strictly less than the parent substory's word count. The maximum stack depth must be at least 3. Because every non-base substory has exactly 2 direct child matched substories at the same depth, the boundary-event sequence contains same-level paired child openings and closings; no requirement is made that sibling child texts differ word-for-word.
verify_steps: Extract every exact boundary sentence "Once it was told." and "So the telling returns." in order; push on each opener and pop on each closer, confirming depth never becomes negative, final depth is 0, maximum depth is at least 3, and there is exactly 1 top-level matched pair.
For each matched pair, count its directly contained child matched pairs and confirm the count is exactly 0 or exactly 2; confirm that every 2-child pair has its 2 children at the same parent depth.

For each 0-child pair, count exactly 1 occurrence of "This is the smallest matter."; for each 2-child pair, confirm that sentence occurs 0 times in the text directly inside the pair but outside its child spans.
Count words in every matched span using maximal runs of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens, and confirm every child span has a strictly smaller word count than its parent span.
recursion.distinguish: Unlike nesting, every opener is matched by a closer and the final stack is empty; unlike symmetry, the required 0-or-2 recursive branching creates same-level paired matched substories inside the stack rather than a single word-for-word mirror sequence.

nesting.device_en: Only-Entering Device: the text contains N opening sentences with N >= 3 and zero closing sentences. Each opening sentence must have the exact form "Name at Place said: \"Once upon a time...\"" where Name and Place are single capitalized letter-only tokens, and every Name and Place token used in an opening sentence is unique across all openings. Opening sentence k+1 must occur after opening sentence k, and because there are no closing sentences, it is inside the story opened by sentence k. After opening sentence k+1 begins, every outer token from levels 1 through k, meaning each earlier Name and Place, must occur exactly 0 times in the remaining text. The exact closing sentence "So the telling returns." must occur exactly 0 times in the whole text. The final sentence of the whole text must occur after opening sentence N and must contain the Name or Place token from opening sentence N at least once, so the text ends at the deepest level.
verify_steps: Count opening sentences matching "Name at Place said: \"Once upon a time...\"" and confirm N >= 3; record each level's Name and Place and confirm all recorded tokens are unique.
Confirm the openings appear in order and count exactly 0 occurrences of the closing sentence "So the telling returns.".
For each k from 1 to N-1, inspect the text after opening k+1 begins and confirm every Name and Place from levels 1 through k occurs 0 times there.
Confirm the final sentence is after opening N and contains the Name or Place token from opening N at least once.
nesting.distinguish: Unlike recursion, which requires matched opener-closer pairs and level-by-level popping, this device has exactly 0 occurrences of the closer "So the telling returns." and forbids any outer proper-name return.

cycle.device_en: Causal Closed-Ring Device: the story is divided into n paragraphs, where a paragraph is a maximal nonempty block of text separated from the next paragraph by one or more blank lines, and n must be at least 3. A sentence is a maximal substring within one paragraph that starts either at the first character of the paragraph or at the first character after the single space following the previous sentence-ending mark, contains no period, question mark, or exclamation mark before its end, and ends in exactly one of ".", "?", or "!"; consecutive sentences inside a paragraph must be separated by exactly one space. A word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens, and two sentences are word-for-word identical if they have the same number of words and the kth word is the exact same string in both sentences for every k. Each paragraph must contain at least 2 sentences. Every sentence must begin with the exact prefix "[L1] "; no word token of the form L followed by one or more digits may occur anywhere except as the sentence-initial word token "L1" in that exact prefix. For paragraph i, let E_i be its first sentence, let R_i be its last sentence, and set E_{n+1}=E_1. Each E_i and each R_i must begin with the exact prefix "[L1] And so ", where "And so" is the explicit causal connector. Define the event A_i as the word-token sequence of E_i after deleting its first 3 word tokens, which must be exactly "L1", "And", and "so"; each A_i must contain at least 1 word, and A_1 through A_n must be pairwise different, so the segment-events are mutually distinct. For every i from 1 through n, R_i must be word-for-word identical to E_{i+1}; in particular, R_n itself, not a substring of R_n, must be word-for-word identical to E_1, giving E_1 -> E_2 -> ... -> E_n -> E_1. For the mirror exclusion, for every integer j with 2 <= j < n + 1 - j <= n - 1, A_j must not be word-for-word identical to A_{n+1-j}; if there is no such j, this condition passes. One full lap restores the starting event without growth, escalation, or flip because every causal result sentence uses the same exact connector prefix "[L1] And so " and R_n has exactly the same word sequence as E_1.
verify_steps: Split the text into maximal nonempty paragraphs separated by one or more blank lines; count n and confirm n >= 3; split each paragraph into sentences under the stated sentence rule and confirm each paragraph has at least 2 sentences.
Confirm every sentence begins with exactly "[L1] "; count word tokens of the form L followed by one or more digits and confirm they occur only as the sentence-initial token "L1" in that prefix.

Extract each paragraph's first sentence E_i and last sentence R_i; confirm each begins with exactly "[L1] And so "; form A_i by deleting the first 3 word tokens "L1", "And", and "so" from E_i, confirm each A_i has at least 1 word, and confirm A_1 through A_n are pairwise different.

For each i from 1 through n, compare R_i word-for-word with E_{i+1}, using E_1 after E_n; then for every integer j with 2 <= j < n + 1 - j <= n - 1, compare A_j with A_{n+1-j} and confirm they are not word-for-word identical.
cycle.distinguish: Unlike strange_loop this requires only sentence-initial "[L1]" level tags and forbids every other L-plus-digits level token, unlike spiral or mobius R_n is word-for-word identical to E_1 with the same connector and no changed return string, unlike symmetry the internal event sequences A_2 through A_{n-1} cannot match at mirrored positions, and n >= 3 separates it from alternation.

symmetry.device_en:
Mirror Palindrome / Crab-Canon Device: The raw story text T uses U+000A as its only line separator and may have one optional final U+000A; define S by deleting exactly one final U+000A from T if T ends with U+000A, and deleting nothing otherwise. S must equal exactly L1 + "
" + L2 + "
" + ... + "
" + Ln for some odd n = 2k+1 with integer k >= 1, with no characters before L1, no characters after Ln, and no empty line. For every i from 1 to n, Li must start exactly with the decimal numeral i followed by ". ", and the text after that label must contain at least 1 word, where a word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens. The story is a single formal narrative layer: in the text after each numeric label, none of these exact case-sensitive substrings may occur: "ENTER LEVEL", "EXIT LEVEL", "BEGIN STORY WITHIN STORY", "END STORY WITHIN STORY", "Level +1", "Level -1", "[enter]", "[exit]". For each line i, let Wi be the ordered list of words in the text after the required numeric label. The unique unpaired center sentence is line k+1. For every j from 1 to k, W(k+1+j) must equal W(k+1−j) word-for-word, except that the two exact character-name words "Alice" and "Bob" may be interchanged: specifically, W(k+1+j) must equal either W(k+1−j) exactly, or the list obtained from W(k+1−j) by replacing every word exactly equal to "Alice" with "Bob" and every word exactly equal to "Bob" with "Alice". Thus line k+2 matches line k, line k+3 matches line k−1, and so on through line n matching line 1; only sentence positions are reversed, not the word order inside any sentence.
verify_steps: Check the raw text T: if it ends with one or more U+000A characters, delete exactly one final U+000A to form S; otherwise use T as S. Split S on U+000A into lines L1..Ln, reconstruct L1 + "\n" + ... + "\n" + Ln, and confirm it equals S exactly, with no empty line.

Count n and confirm n = 2k+1 for an integer k >= 1; for every i from 1 to n, confirm Li starts exactly with the decimal numeral i followed by ". ", and confirm the text after that label contains at least 1 word.

In the text after every numeric label, search for the exact forbidden substrings "ENTER LEVEL", "EXIT LEVEL", "BEGIN STORY WITHIN STORY", "END STORY WITHIN STORY", "Level +1", "Level -1", "[enter]", and "[exit]"; reject if any occurrence is found.

For every line i, extract its ordered word list Wi; for each j from 1 to k, compare W(k+1+j) with W(k+1−j), accepting the pair only if the lists are identical or if the later list is exactly the earlier list after the defined word-level swap of "Alice" and "Bob".
symmetry.distinguish: Unlike figure-ground same-order retelling, this device compares k+1+j to k+1−j in reverse positional order, and unlike recursion, it mechanically forbids the exact layer-entry, layer-exit, and story-within-story marker substrings listed in the device.

alternation.device_en: Two-Voice Alternation in script form: define a physical line by splitting the complete story text at newline characters; if the text ends with a newline character, the final zero-character segment also counts as a physical line. The complete story text must contain exactly N physical lines, where N = 2k, 8 <= N <= 20, and N is not 2000. A blank physical line is defined as either a zero-character line or a line consisting only of U+0020 space characters and/or U+0009 tab characters; the text must contain exactly 0 blank physical lines. Each physical line is one dialogue line and must have character 1 equal to "A" or "B", character 2 equal to ":", and no character before character 1; the first two characters of every line must therefore be exactly "A:" or exactly "B:". No physical line may begin with any other two-character string, so there are 0 narration lines and 0 third-speaker lines. Number the physical lines from 1 to N: line i must begin with "A:" if and only if i is odd, and line i must begin with "B:" if and only if i is even. Thus adjacent lines always have different labels, and any two lines whose indices differ by 2 always have the same label; there are exactly 0 exceptions.
verify_steps: Split the complete story text at newline characters into physical lines, counting a final zero-character segment if the text ends with a newline; count N and confirm N is even, 8 <= N <= 20, and N is not 2000.
For every physical line, count its characters and confirm it is not zero characters and not composed only of U+0020 spaces and/or U+0009 tabs.
For every physical line, extract character 1 and character 2 and confirm character 1 is exactly "A" or exactly "B", character 2 is exactly ":", and there is no character before character 1.

Number the physical lines from 1 to N and compare labels with parity: every odd-numbered line begins with exactly "A:", every even-numbered line begins with exactly "B:", every adjacent pair has different labels, and every pair whose indices differ by 2 has identical labels.
alternation.distinguish: Unlike longer-cycle motifs, this device requires exactly the two labels "A:" and "B:" with label i equal to label i+2 wherever both exist; unlike anomaly motifs, it allows exactly 0 parity exceptions; unlike narration or third-voice motifs, every physical line must start at character 1 with exactly "A:" or exactly "B:".

spiral.device_en: Spiral Refrain: use the fixed core phrase "Round and round again" as the refrain; this core phrase has exactly 4 words, where a word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens. For all checks, first replace every CRLF pair with LF and then replace every remaining CR with LF; a line is the sequence of characters between two LF characters, before the first LF, or after the last LF, and a paragraph is a maximal consecutive sequence of 1 or more nonempty lines, with its paragraph text equal to those lines joined by single LF characters. Exact string comparison uses Unicode code points with no case folding and no normalization. The exact string "Round and round again" must occur exactly 4 times in the whole converted story. Each of the 4 occurrences must begin at character position 1 of a different paragraph text, so each occurrence starts its paragraph; these 4 paragraphs are the refrain paragraphs in order of appearance. The 4 refrain paragraphs must have exactly 6, 12, 24, and 48 words, respectively, so each count is exactly 2 times the previous count. Refrain paragraph 1 must contain the exact string "one person" at least 1 time; refrain paragraph 2 must contain the exact string "one family" at least 1 time; refrain paragraph 3 must contain the exact string "one village" at least 1 time; refrain paragraph 4 must contain the exact string "one kingdom" at least 1 time. No 2 refrain paragraphs may have the same word count. The 4 refrain paragraphs must be 4 distinct top-level paragraphs in the single paragraph sequence, and their paragraph indices must be strictly increasing.
verify_steps: Normalize line endings by replacing CRLF with LF and then lone CR with LF; split the story into lines, split the lines into maximal paragraph blocks separated by one or more empty lines, and number the resulting paragraphs 1, 2, 3, and so on.

Using exact Unicode code point matching with no normalization, confirm that "Round and round again" has exactly 4 words under the stated word rule, occurs exactly 4 times in the converted story, and each occurrence begins at character position 1 of a different paragraph text.
For the 4 refrain paragraphs in order of appearance, count words under the stated word rule and confirm the counts are exactly 6, 12, 24, and 48; confirm no 2 of these 4 counts are equal.

Confirm the required scope strings occur in order by refrain paragraph: paragraph 1 contains "one person", paragraph 2 contains "one family", paragraph 3 contains "one village", and paragraph 4 contains "one kingdom"; confirm the 4 refrain paragraph indices are strictly increasing in the single top-level paragraph sequence.
spiral.distinguish: Unlike cycle, spiral requires refrain paragraph word counts 6, 12, 24, and 48 with no equal pair, and unlike nesting, the 4 refrain paragraphs must be distinct top-level paragraphs with strictly increasing paragraph indices in one flat paragraph sequence.

convergence.device_en: Three-Line Convergence: the story has exactly three separately labeled lines that remain name-disjoint until one terminal meeting sentence. The story text is ASCII only, and all string and token comparisons are case-sensitive. The whole text must have the exact form P1 LF LF P2 LF LF P3 LF LF P4 LF LF P5 LF LF P6 LF LF P7, where LF is U+000A, each Pi is nonempty, no Pi contains LF, and there is no character before P1 or after P7; equivalently there are exactly 7 paragraphs and exactly 12 LF characters forming exactly 6 paragraph separators. Sentences are parsed separately inside each paragraph by this deterministic rule: scan left to right; a sentence begins at paragraph character 1 or immediately after the exact two-character separator ". "; it ends at the next "."; the sentence body before that period has length at least 1, contains no "." and no LF, begins with a non-space character, and ends with a non-space character; if the ending period is not the final character of the paragraph, it is followed by exactly one space; the final character of every paragraph is "."; the whole story contains exactly 0 occurrences of "!" and exactly 0 occurrences of "?". A word token is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens; a proper-name token for this device is any word token containing at least one uppercase letter A-Z; a named string occurs only when a word token equals it exactly. Paragraphs 1 through 6 begin with the exact three-character labels "A: ", "B: ", "C: ", "A: ", "B: ", "C: " respectively; paragraph 7 has length at least 2 and its first two characters are not "A:", not "B:", and not "C:". The A-line proper names are exactly the person-name "Alice" and the place-name "Oakmere"; the B-line proper names are exactly the person-name "Bruno" and the place-name "Redhill"; the C-line proper names are exactly the person-name "Clara" and the place-name "Graymarket"; the convergence place-name is "Stonewell"; these 7 strings are pairwise unequal. In each A-labeled paragraph, the first word token is exactly "A", the word token "A" occurs exactly 1 time, "Alice" occurs at least 1 time, "Oakmere" occurs at least 1 time, and every proper-name token is one of "A", "Alice", or "Oakmere". In each B-labeled paragraph, the first word token is exactly "B", the word token "B" occurs exactly 1 time, "Bruno" occurs at least 1 time, "Redhill" occurs at least 1 time, and every proper-name token is one of "B", "Bruno", or "Redhill". In each C-labeled paragraph, the first word token is exactly "C", the word token "C" occurs exactly 1 time, "Clara" occurs at least 1 time, "Graymarket" occurs at least 1 time, and every proper-name token is one of "C", "Clara", or "Graymarket". Paragraph 7 contains exactly 0 word tokens equal to "A", exactly 0 word tokens equal to "B", and exactly 0 word tokens equal to "C". Let F be the final parsed sentence of paragraph 7. In every parsed sentence before F, after ignoring the paragraph-initial label token "A", "B", or "C" when such a label token is present, all remaining proper-name tokens are either a subset of {"Alice", "Oakmere"}, or a subset of {"Bruno", "Redhill"}, or a subset of {"Clara", "Graymarket"}, or the empty set; additionally, every parsed sentence before F contains at most 1 of the 3 person-name tokens "Alice", "Bruno", and "Clara". The word token "Stonewell" occurs exactly 0 times before F. Sentence F contains "Alice" at least 1 time, "Bruno" at least 1 time, "Clara" at least 1 time, and "Stonewell" at least 1 time, and every proper-name token in F is one of "Alice", "Bruno", "Clara", or "Stonewell". The period ending F is the final character of paragraph 7 and the final character of the whole story.
verify_steps: Confirm ASCII-only text; decompose the text exactly as P1 LF LF P2 LF LF P3 LF LF P4 LF LF P5 LF LF P6 LF LF P7 with each Pi nonempty and LF-free; then parse every paragraph into sentences by the stated left-to-right period rule, confirming one-space sentence separators, final periods, and 0 occurrences of "!" and "?".

Tokenize the text into word tokens; identify proper-name tokens as tokens containing A-Z; confirm the paragraph labels "A: ", "B: ", "C: ", "A: ", "B: ", "C: " on paragraphs 1-6 and no "A:", "B:", or "C:" start on paragraph 7.

For paragraphs 1-6, count exact word tokens and proper-name tokens: each labeled paragraph has exactly its label token once as first word token, contains its own person-name and place-name at least once, and contains no proper-name token outside that line’s allowed label/person/place set.

Let F be the final sentence of paragraph 7; confirm paragraph 7 has 0 tokens "A", "B", and "C"; confirm every sentence before F has remaining proper-name tokens from at most one line set and at most one of "Alice", "Bruno", "Clara"; confirm "Stonewell" occurs 0 times before F; confirm F contains "Alice", "Bruno", "Clara", and "Stonewell" at least once, contains no other proper-name token, and is followed by 0 characters.
convergence.distinguish: Unlike bottleneck, convergence requires the first all-three person-name co-occurrence and the first occurrence of the shared place-name "Stonewell" to be in the final sentence with 0 characters after it, while all earlier sentences remain restricted to at most one line’s proper-name set.

bottleneck.device_en: Gate Sentence Bottleneck: the story has exactly 3 threads named "CARAVAN", "MESSENGER", and "FUGITIVE"; each thread is told in exactly 5 labeled segments, and every segment begins with a label of the form "THREAD — LOCATION:" using one of those 3 thread names. In each thread's 5-location sequence, the location "Log Bridge" appears exactly once and must be the 3rd location, so each thread has exactly 2 labeled locations before "Log Bridge" and exactly 2 labeled locations after it. Apart from "Log Bridge", the 3 threads' location names must be pairwise disjoint: no non-bridge location label may occur in more than one thread. In the segment labeled with location "Log Bridge" for each of the 3 threads, the exact sentence "To cross the river, the only way is that log bridge." must appear once; that exact sentence must appear exactly 3 times in the whole story. The final line of the whole story must be the exact tail note sentence "The next year the bridge fell, and the two shores were never joined again."
verify_steps: Group the labeled segments by the thread names "CARAVAN", "MESSENGER", and "FUGITIVE" and confirm each thread has exactly 5 segments.
For each thread, list the 5 location labels in order and confirm "Log Bridge" appears exactly once and exactly in position 3.
Compare all non-bridge location labels across the 3 threads and confirm no non-bridge location label occurs in more than one thread.

Search for the exact sentence "To cross the river, the only way is that log bridge." and confirm it appears once in each "Log Bridge" segment and exactly 3 times total; then confirm the final line is exactly "The next year the bridge fell, and the two shores were never joined again."
bottleneck.distinguish: Unlike convergence, bottleneck has two later locations after the shared point in every thread, and unlike hub it has two locations before and two locations after the center in every thread rather than endpoints only one step from the center.

symmetry_breaking.device_en: One Law, One Break: the whole story has exactly 12 sentences. A sentence is any stretch of text ending in '.', '!', or '?' and containing no other '.', '!', or '?'. A word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens. Sentences 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 must each contain exactly 7 words and must each contain the word "wind" at least once, matched case-insensitively as a whole word. Sentence 7 alone must contain exactly 8 words and must contain zero whole-word occurrences of "wind" in any case. Thus the unique violation is precisely sentence 7 and every other sentence obeys the same 7-word-with-wind rule.
verify_steps: Split the story into sentences by '.', '!', and '?' and confirm there are exactly 12 sentences with no extra sentence-ending marks inside a sentence.
Count words in every sentence and confirm sentences 1-6 and 8-12 each have exactly 7 words, while sentence 7 has exactly 8 words.
Search each sentence for whole-word "wind" case-insensitively and confirm sentences 1-6 and 8-12 contain it at least once, while sentence 7 contains it zero times.
Confirm no sentence other than sentence 7 violates either the word-count rule or the "wind" rule.
symmetry_breaking.distinguish: Unlike tiling or alternation, symmetry_breaking requires exactly one mechanically locatable violation, sentence 7, while those devices require zero violations everywhere.

strange_loop.device_en: Device: three-level strange-loop narration. The story must contain exactly three narration blocks, introduced exactly once each by the verbatim labels "A says:", "B says:", and "C says:", in that order; the labels themselves do not count as sentences. A narration block is the text immediately after one label up to the next label or the end of the story. Sentence counting uses periods only: a sentence is a maximal substring ending in ".". Block 1 must contain exactly one sentence, and that sentence must be exactly "A is telling B's story." Block 2 must contain exactly one sentence, and that sentence must be exactly "B is telling C's story." Block 3 must contain exactly two sentences; its first sentence must be exactly "The protagonist is A." and its last sentence must be exactly "A is telling B's story." The token A in Block 3's first sentence must be the same exact name token as the token A in Block 1's sentence.
verify_steps: Find the exact labels "A says:", "B says:", and "C says:" and confirm that each appears exactly once and in that order.
Split the text into three narration blocks using those labels, then count sentences in each block by periods only.
Check that Block 1 has exactly one sentence, "A is telling B's story.", and Block 2 has exactly one sentence, "B is telling C's story."

Check that Block 3 has exactly two sentences; its first sentence is "The protagonist is A." and its last sentence is "A is telling B's story."; then compare the A token in Block 3 with the A token in Block 1 for exact equality.
strange_loop.distinguish: Unlike cycle, the return is a cross-block narrator chain rather than same-block causality; unlike nesting, the deepest block lands back on the outer opener by repeating "A is telling B's story." verbatim; unlike self_reference, the back-reference is mediated by the two intervening labels "B says:" and "C says:" rather than a one-step self-copy; unlike recursion, there is no level-by-level unwind, only a single verbatim back-edge from Block 3 to Block 1.

figure_ground.device_en: Device: figure-ground retelling. The story has exactly two named characters, Alice and Beth, and exactly 2m sentences (m >= 2). The same event sequence is told twice in the same order. In sentences 1..m Alice is the grammatical subject of every sentence (the sentence's first noun, before the main verb) and Beth never appears as a subject -- she appears only after the main verb (object or prepositional slot), exactly once per sentence. In sentences m+1..2m the roles are exactly complementary: sentence m+i has the SAME main verb as sentence i and describes the same event in the same position of the sequence, but Beth is the subject and Alice appears only after the verb, exactly once. The order of events in the second half is identical to the first half (not reversed). Other words may differ freely as long as the main verb of each pair matches word-for-word. Normal English capitalization is allowed.
verify_steps: Count sentences: exactly 2m with m >= 2.

For i in 1..m: sentence i starts with 'Alice' as subject and contains 'Beth' exactly once, after the main verb; sentence m+i starts with 'Beth' as subject and contains 'Alice' exactly once, after the main verb.
For each pair (i, m+i): extract the main verb (first verb after the subject); the two verbs must be identical word-for-word, and the pairs must appear in the same order in both halves.
Confirm the second half does NOT reverse the order of events (verb sequence of second half equals that of first half, not its reversal).
figure_ground.distinguish: Figure-ground swaps subject and object roles ONCE at the midpoint while keeping event order and vocabulary; it is not a palindrome (order not reversed), not isomorphism (one cast, one domain, no dictionary between two systems), not alternation (the swap happens once, not sentence by sentence), and not duality (the swap is figure/ground of the SAME telling, not an involutive re-derivation of each sentence).

isomorphism.device_en: Device: parallel scrolls of two worlds. The story begins with exactly this replacement table, in this order: "woodcutter=old-wolf; daylight=black-night; climb-hill=enter-forest; axe=claw; cabin=den; bread=bone." After the table, the story contains exactly 12 sentences split into an upper half of sentences 1-6 and a lower half of sentences 7-12. For each k from 1 to 6, sentence 6+k must be obtained from sentence k by replacing every whole-word occurrence of "woodcutter" with "old-wolf", "daylight" with "black-night", "climb-hill" with "enter-forest", "axe" with "claw", "cabin" with "den", and "bread" with "bone", while leaving every word not in the table unchanged. The table must be bijective: the 6 left-side words are all different, the 6 right-side words are all different, and no left-side word equals any right-side word. The sentence order is not reversed: upper sentence 1 maps to lower sentence 7, 2 to 8, 3 to 9, 4 to 10, 5 to 11, and 6 to 12. The device fails if any table word is translated differently, if two source words share one target word, if one source word has two target words, or if any non-table word changes.
verify_steps: Confirm the opening table is exactly "woodcutter=old-wolf; daylight=black-night; climb-hill=enter-forest; axe=claw; cabin=den; bread=bone."
Check bijection: count 6 distinct left-side words, 6 distinct right-side words, and zero overlap between the two sides.
Count exactly 12 post-table sentences and split them into sentences 1-6 and 7-12.
For each k from 1 to 6, apply the table word by word to sentence k and compare the result word-for-word with sentence 6+k.
isomorphism.distinguish: Unlike symmetry, this maps sentence k to sentence k rather than reversing around a midpoint; unlike figure_ground, the halves use disjoint world-words carried by a complete dictionary rather than swapping two roles inside one story.

mobius.device_en: Device: two-lap involution closure. The story has exactly 9 sentences: sentences 1-4 form the first lap, sentences 5-8 form the second lap, and sentence 9 is the epilogue. The only allowed orientation-word swap is the fixed involution "left" <-> "right", "inside" <-> "outside", and "above" <-> "below"; the swap applies only to whole-word tokens and leaves every other word unchanged. Sentences 1-4 and sentences 5-8 are aligned in the same order, not reversed: for each i from 1 to 4, sentence 4+i must be word-for-word identical to sentence i after applying that swap exactly once. The first lap must contain at least 3 orientation-word tokens in total, and the second lap must contain at least 3 orientation-word tokens in total. Sentence 5 must not be word-for-word identical to sentence 1, so one lap does not close. Sentence 9 must be word-for-word identical to sentence 1, so two laps do close. Applying the same swap twice to sentences 1-4 must restore sentences 1-4 exactly, because the swap is its own inverse.
verify_steps: Count exactly 9 sentences and split them into sentences 1-4, 5-8, and 9.
Count whole-word tokens from the set {"left", "right", "inside", "outside", "above", "below"} in sentences 1-4, and separately in sentences 5-8; each lap must have at least 3 such tokens.

For each i from 1 to 4, swap each whole-word occurrence of "left"/"right", "inside"/"outside", and "above"/"below" in sentence i exactly once, then compare the result word-for-word with sentence 4+i; also confirm sentence 5 is not identical to sentence 1.
Apply the same swap a second time to sentences 1-4 and compare the results word-for-word with sentences 1-4; then compare sentence 9 word-for-word with sentence 1 and confirm they are identical.
mobius.distinguish: Unlike symmetry, the second lap is not reversed; unlike isomorphism, the swap is a self-inverse orientation flip within one story; unlike cycle, one lap does not close; unlike alternation, the flip happens by lap, not by alternating events.

braiding.device_en: Braiding seating-permutation device: the story has at least 2 paragraphs, and every paragraph has exactly 2 sentences. The first sentence of every paragraph must be exactly "Current seating: X-Y-Z." where X, Y, and Z are the three role labels currently in seats 1, 2, and 3, in that order. The second sentence of every paragraph must be the only swap sentence in that paragraph, and it must be exactly one of these two verbatim forms: "Swap seats 1 and 2: A passes over B." or "Swap seats 2 and 3: A passes over B."; in the seat-1/2 form, A must be the label in seat 1 and B must be the label in seat 2 immediately before the swap, and in the seat-2/3 form, A must be the label in seat 2 and B must be the label in seat 3 immediately before the swap. For every paragraph, the next paragraph's opening seating must equal the seating obtained by applying that paragraph's swap to its opening seating. Across the whole story, at least one paragraph must use a seat-1/2 swap and at least one paragraph must use a seat-2/3 swap, and the final seating must not be identical to the first paragraph's opening seating.
verify_steps: Count the paragraphs and the sentences in each paragraph; confirm there are at least 2 paragraphs and exactly 2 sentences per paragraph.

For every paragraph, check that sentence 1 is exactly "Current seating: X-Y-Z." and sentence 2 is exactly one of the two allowed swap sentences, with no extra swap sentence in that paragraph; extract X, Y, Z and the seat position and labels named in the swap sentence.

Starting from paragraph 1's seating, verify that the swap sentence in paragraph 1 names the actual occupants of the stated seats before the swap, then apply each paragraph's swap in order and confirm that each next paragraph's opening seating matches the computed result.

Confirm that at least one swap sentence is of the 1-and-2 type and at least one is of the 2-and-3 type, and confirm that the final computed seating is not identical to the first paragraph's opening seating.
braiding.distinguish: Unlike alternation, this composes two distinct adjacent swap positions on three seats in sequence rather than alternating two states; unlike cycle or symmetry, the checker follows the step-by-step product of swaps, requires the first swap's labels to match the actual initial occupants, and requires the final seating to differ from the initial seating.

interference.device_en: Device: 3-against-4 interference over two full least-common-multiple cycles. The story must contain exactly 24 sentences, numbered 1 through 24 in order; for this device, each occurrence of '.', '?', or '!' ends one sentence, and commas, semicolons, colons, quotation marks, parentheses, dashes, and line breaks do not end sentences. A word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens. For every sentence whose number is a multiple of 3, namely 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21, and 24, the first word must be exactly "Again" with uppercase A and lowercase gain; for every sentence whose number is not a multiple of 3, the first word must not be exactly "Again" with that same case-sensitive spelling. The final clause of a sentence is the stretch after the last comma, semicolon, or colon in that sentence, excluding the final '.', '?', or '!'; if the sentence contains no comma, semicolon, or colon, the whole sentence excluding final punctuation is its final clause. For every sentence whose number is a multiple of 4, namely 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, and 24, the final clause must contain exactly 7 words; for every sentence whose number is not a multiple of 4, the final clause must not contain exactly 7 words. The A-hit set must be exactly {3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24}, the B-hit set must be exactly {4,8,12,16,20,24}, and their intersection must be exactly {12,24}; the gap between the two overlap positions is exactly 12, which is lcm(3,4). The story must continue past the first overlap by having sentences 13 through 24 after sentence 12.
verify_steps: Scan the story, count each occurrence of '.', '?', or '!' as ending one sentence, ignore commas, semicolons, colons, quotation marks, parentheses, dashes, and line breaks as sentence endings, and verify that exactly 24 numbered sentences result.
For each sentence, extract the first word using the word definition and mark A if it is exactly the case-sensitive string "Again"; verify that the A-hit set is exactly {3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24}.

For each sentence, take the final clause as the text after the last comma, semicolon, or colon, or the whole sentence if none appears, excluding final punctuation; count its words and mark B if it contains exactly 7 words; verify that the B-hit set is exactly {4,8,12,16,20,24}.
Intersect the A-hit set and B-hit set and verify that the double-hit set is exactly {12,24}, that 24 - 12 = 12, and that sentences 13 through 24 exist after sentence 12.
interference.distinguish: Unlike alternation, the double-hit gap is 12 rather than 2; unlike convergence, the first double hit at sentence 12 is not terminal because sentences 13 through 24 must exist after it.

tiling.device_en: Device: seamless template tiling by 8 adjacent shifted copies. The whole story must consist of exactly 8 consecutive tile instances and no other characters: 0 characters before tile 1, 0 characters between tile k and tile k+1 for k = 1 through 7, and 0 characters after tile 8. Each tile instance must have exactly this character-level template, where each slot is exactly 1 word: PERSON slot, then the verbatim substring " carried the ", then OBJECT slot, then the verbatim substring " from ", then PLACE slot, then the verbatim substring " to the mill gate.". A word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens; the final period is punctuation after the word "gate" and is not part of any word. In every tile, the PERSON slot, OBJECT slot, and PLACE slot are the only variable substrings; every non-slot substring must be character-for-character identical to the quoted substrings, including casing, spaces, and the final period. Each tile therefore contains exactly 10 words, exactly 9 U+0020 spaces, and exactly 1 period; the whole story contains exactly 80 words, exactly 72 U+0020 spaces, and exactly 8 periods. For the shift-copy check, replace the 3 slot words in each tile with the labels "PERSON", "OBJECT", and "PLACE"; the resulting 8 masked tile strings must be exactly identical, so shifting the masked pattern by exactly 1 tile makes tile k coincide character-for-character with tile k+1 for k = 1 through 7. No character may belong to more than 1 tile, and every character of the story must belong to exactly 1 tile.
verify_steps: Starting at character 1, parse exactly 8 consecutive tiles of the form: 1 word, " carried the ", 1 word, " from ", 1 word, " to the mill gate."; verify that the final character of tile 8 is the final character of the story.
For each tile, count exactly 10 words, exactly 9 U+0020 spaces, and exactly 1 period; for the whole story, count exactly 80 words, exactly 72 U+0020 spaces, and exactly 8 periods.

For each boundary k = 1 through 7, verify that the character immediately after the period ending tile k is the first character of the PERSON slot of tile k+1, with 0 intervening characters; verify 0 characters before tile 1 and 0 characters after tile 8.
In each tile, replace the PERSON, OBJECT, and PLACE slot words with "PERSON", "OBJECT", and "PLACE" and compare the 8 masked tile strings; verify that all 8 are character-for-character identical.
tiling.distinguish: Unlike alternation this has 1 masked template repeated for all 8 tiles rather than 2 alternating templates, unlike symmetry_breaking it permits exactly 0 exceptions, and unlike isomorphism it requires character-for-character shifted copies within one text rather than a mapping between two systems.

hub.device_en: Device: Miller-Relay Hub, a counted-speech-record device whose required checks are the exact label list, the record format, and the ordered-pair tests in this paragraph. The center label is exactly "the miller"; the five villager labels are exactly "Villager A", "Villager B", "Villager C", "Villager D", and "Villager E". A counted speech record consists of these raw characters in this order: left square bracket U+005B; one speaker label chosen from the 6 allowed labels; the exact separator string space-hyphen-greater-than-space, U+0020 U+002D U+003E U+0020; one listener label chosen from the 6 allowed labels; right square bracket U+005D; one space U+0020; left double quotation mark U+201C; a message; right double quotation mark U+201D. In every counted speech record, the speaker label and listener label must be different, and the message must contain at least 1 word token, where a word token is a maximal run of letters A-Z or a-z, digits 0-9, apostrophes U+0027, or hyphens U+002D. The story must contain 0 straight double quotation marks U+0022. Every occurrence of U+201C or U+201D in the story must be one of the two quotation delimiters of a counted speech record. Every bracketed arrow tag in the story, defined as a substring from U+005B to the next U+005D that contains the exact separator string U+0020 U+002D U+003E U+0020, must be the tag of a counted speech record with allowed labels. Extract from every counted speech record, in story order, the ordered pair (speaker, listener). Every extracted ordered pair must contain "the miller" as speaker or listener. No extracted ordered pair may have both speaker and listener chosen from the 5 villager labels. For each of "Villager A", "Villager B", "Villager C", "Villager D", and "Villager E", the total number of extracted ordered pairs in which that villager appears as speaker or listener must be at least 1. At least 1 extracted ordered pair must have "the miller" as listener, and at least 1 extracted ordered pair must have "the miller" as speaker.
verify_steps: Scan the story for speech-record syntax: verify 0 occurrences of straight double quotation mark U+0022; verify every U+201C and U+201D is paired as the delimiter of a counted speech record; verify every bracketed arrow tag containing the exact separator string U+0020 U+002D U+003E U+0020 is a counted speech record tag.
For each counted speech record, verify the speaker and listener are two different labels from exactly the 6 allowed labels, and verify the message contains at least 1 word token as defined.
Extract all ordered pairs (speaker, listener) in story order; verify every pair contains "the miller" as one of its two entries, and verify no pair has villager labels in both entries.

For each of the 5 villager labels, count appearances as speaker plus appearances as listener and verify the total is at least 1; also verify at least 1 pair has "the miller" as listener and at least 1 pair has "the miller" as speaker.
hub.distinguish: Unlike bottleneck, the clause requiring every extracted ordered pair to contain "the miller" makes the center a communication endpoint rather than a crossed midpoint between two banks; unlike convergence, the clauses requiring at least 1 pair with "the miller" as listener and at least 1 pair with "the miller" as speaker rule out a one-way list of lines that only enter a terminal sink.

diagonalization.device_en: Device: the diagonal escape. The story must list an integer n with n >= 4, then exactly n numbered storytellers labeled 1 through n, then exactly n numbered binary features labeled 1 through n. Each storyteller row must give exactly n feature values, each value being exactly "day" or exactly "night". After those n rows, the story must give exactly one additional row labeled "Nameless Traveler" with exactly n feature values. For every k from 1 through n, the Nameless Traveler's feature k must be the opposite of storyteller k's feature k: "day" flips to "night" and "night" flips to "day". The Nameless Traveler row must not contain any of the exact strings "this story", "this sentence", "this tale", or "itself". The story must contain exactly one table of feature rows, no second table, no row whose label is repeated, and no row nested inside another row. Convention: row/section labels (numerals or names introducing each storyteller) are labels, not words -- exclude them from all word counts and feature extraction; each storyteller's row consists of exactly the n feature words after its label.
verify_steps: Read n, verify n >= 4, and verify that there are exactly n storyteller rows labeled 1 through n plus exactly one row labeled "Nameless Traveler".
Verify that each row has exactly n feature values and that every feature value is exactly "day" or "night". (exclude labels from all counts)
For each k from 1 through n, compare storyteller k's feature k with the Nameless Traveler's feature k and verify that the two values are opposites. (exclude labels from all counts)

Verify that the Nameless Traveler row lacks "this story", "this sentence", "this tale", and "itself", and that the feature table occurs exactly once with no repeated row label. (exclude labels from all counts)
diagonalization.distinguish: Unlike self_reference the new row is barred from the self-pointing strings, unlike recursion and nesting there is exactly one unnested table, and unlike symmetry_breaking there are n systematic diagonal differences, one against each row at position k.

infinite_descent.device_en: Device: lawsuit of infinite descent against an heirloom claim. The story has exactly 7 sentences total: sentences 1-6 are citation sentences, and sentence 7 is the elder's judgment. Each citation sentence must be an independent sentence with exactly one speaker label of the form `Holder N` and exactly one pointed-to holder label of the form `Holder M`; the sentence must use the exact relation phrase `points to`, and the only positive-integer Arabic numerals in that sentence must be `N` and `M`, with `N > M`. Across the 6 citation sentences, the 6 pointed-to numbers `M` must form a strictly decreasing sequence. The 6 pointed-to numbers must not form a fixed-ratio progression: at least one adjacent triple `a, b, c` among them must satisfy `a*c != b*b`. The final sentence must be the elder's judgment and must contain the exact phrase `never existed` or the exact phrase `impossible`; it must explicitly state that the first claimant/holder did not exist, so the entire chain is void from its beginning rather than reaching any base case or returning from one. No citation sentence may point to more than one earlier holder, no sentence may describe the chain as converging to an actually existing endpoint, and no sentence may rely on any conserved quantity or parity/odd-even argument.
verify_steps: Count the sentences and verify there are exactly 7, with sentences 1-6 serving as citation sentences and sentence 7 serving as the elder's judgment.
For each of sentences 1-6, verify that it contains exactly one `points to` relation, exactly one `Holder N` speaker label, exactly one `Holder M` target label, and that `N > M`.
Extract the 6 target numbers `M` from sentences 1-6 and verify that they are strictly decreasing; then check that at least one adjacent triple `a, b, c` among those 6 numbers satisfies `a*c != b*b`.

Check that sentence 7 contains `never existed` or `impossible` and explicitly says that the first claimant/holder did not exist; also check that no sentence uses a base-case/return explanation, a convergence-to-real-endpoint claim, or any conserved-quantity/parity argument.
infinite_descent.distinguish: Unlike recursion, this story forbids any base case or return and instead denies that the first claimant ever existed; unlike zeno_halving, the cited numbers are only required to be strictly decreasing and not a fixed-ratio progression, and the ending is impossibility rather than completion; unlike cascade, each citation points to exactly one earlier holder; unlike contraction_fixed_point, no sentence may describe convergence to an actually existing endpoint; and unlike invariant_barrier, no conserved quantity or parity proof is allowed.

coprime_orbit.device_en: Device: Coprime Orbit at a round table. The story must state exactly 8 seated people labeled with the numerals 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and one lamp; it must state the rule verbatim as "Each time, skip 2 people and hand the lamp to the 3rd person." It must also state verbatim "gcd(3,8)=1" before the successful passing begins. The successful named passing order must be exactly "0, 3, 6, 1, 4, 7, 2, 5, 0": the first 8 labels are the receivers, each of the 8 labels 0 through 7 appears exactly once among them, and the 9th label is 0, returning the lamp to the first receiver. After that order, an elder must say verbatim "Three and eight are coprime, so the lamp misses no one." The contrast trial must state verbatim "gcd(2,8)=2" and must use the proposed rule verbatim "Each time, skip 1 person and hand the lamp to the 2nd person." Its two-lap named order must be exactly "0, 2, 4, 6, 0, 2, 4, 6, 0"; the omitted set must be written exactly as "The people who never receive the lamp are 1, 3, 5, 7." No passing order in the device may be the adjacent order "0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 0", no second independent periodic schedule may be present, and no person or place may be labeled "center", "hub", or "middle".
verify_steps: Find the labels, the two quoted rules, and the two gcd statements; confirm they are exactly the required strings and numbers.
Extract the successful order and compare it word-for-word and number-for-number with "0, 3, 6, 1, 4, 7, 2, 5, 0"; confirm the first 8 entries are a permutation of 0 through 7 and the 9th entry is 0.
Extract the contrast order and compare it with "0, 2, 4, 6, 0, 2, 4, 6, 0"; compare the stated omitted set with "1, 3, 5, 7".
Search for the forbidden adjacent order and for the words "center", "hub", and "middle"; confirm none occur as labels or as the explanation of success.
coprime_orbit.distinguish: It differs from cycle by forbidding the adjacent order, from interference by allowing only one passing schedule, from hub by forbidding any center or hub, and from pigeonhole by requiring the constructive full orbit order.

pigeonhole.device_en: Device: Pigeonhole by months and travelers. The story must state exactly 12 boxes labeled with the 12 month names "January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July", "August", "September", "October", "November", "December" and exactly 13 travelers labeled "Traveler 1" through "Traveler 13". It must state the rule verbatim as "Every traveler belongs to exactly one birth month." Before any traveler-month assignment list appears, an elder must say verbatim "Thirteen is more than twelve, so at least two travelers were born in the same month." Later, and only later, the story must give a complete assignment list of 13 lines, each in the exact form "Traveler X: Month", where X is one of 1 through 13 and Month is one of the 12 month names. In that final assignment list, at least one month name must occur on at least 2 lines. The elder's earlier sentence must not name any traveler number and must not name any month. The assignment list must not put all 13 travelers in the same month.
verify_steps: Count the month labels and traveler labels; confirm there are exactly 12 months and exactly 13 travelers and that the quoted rule appears.
Locate the elder's quoted sentence and confirm it occurs before the first line matching "Traveler X: Month"; confirm that sentence contains no traveler number and no month name.
Count the final assignment lines; confirm there are exactly 13, each traveler number 1 through 13 appears exactly once, and every month is one of the 12 labels.
Count month occurrences in the final list; confirm at least one month occurs at least twice and no single month occurs 13 times.
pigeonhole.distinguish: It differs from convergence by forbidding all 13 travelers in one month and by leaving the collision place unspecified before the reveal, and from bottleneck or hub by using only the count 13>12 rather than a forced path or mediator.

projective_duality.device_en: Device: The Involutive Role-Swap. The story must begin with exactly one first sentence that explicitly lists the swap dictionary, and that sentence must contain exactly n single-word pairs, with n >= 1, written as whole-word pairs in the form "A <-> B" separated by semicolons; every word may appear in exactly one pair, there are no leftover words, and the dictionary is the only allowed substitution map. After that first sentence, the story contains exactly two tellings, labeled on separate lines exactly "Telling One:" and "Telling Two:". Telling One and Telling Two must have the same number of sentences, m, with m >= 1, and sentence i in Telling Two must correspond to sentence i in Telling One in the same order, not reversed. If every whole-word occurrence of each dictionary word in Telling Two is replaced everywhere by its paired word, the result must be word-for-word identical to Telling One, including punctuation and sentence boundaries. The final sentence of the story must be exactly "Swap once more and the original words return.".
verify_steps: Check that the very first sentence is the swap dictionary, that it contains exactly n single-word pairs in the form "A <-> B", that no word appears in more than one pair, and that there are no unpaired items.

Locate the two labels exactly "Telling One:" and "Telling Two:", count the sentences in each telling, and confirm the counts are equal and the sentence order is the same position-by-position, not reversed.
Apply the dictionary to every whole-word occurrence in Telling Two and compare the resulting text to Telling One word-for-word, including punctuation and sentence breaks.
Check that the final sentence is exactly "Swap once more and the original words return.".
projective_duality.distinguish: It differs from isomorphism because the swap dictionary operates inside one story rather than mapping between two different materials; from symmetry because the second telling keeps the same sentence order instead of reversing it; from transformed_canon because it is a direct role-word restatement rather than a delayed transformed voice; from chirality because the two tellings both hold and a second swap restores the original exactly; from figure_ground because nothing relies on negative space or a split canvas; and from mobius because there is no path or lap condition at all.

contraction_fixed_point.device_en:
Device: The Shrinking Return. The story opens with one exact rule sentence: "After each singing, delete the last floor(n/2) words, where n is the current word count." Each of the 7 chant lines is written on its own line as `Round 0:` through `Round 6:`, and the label `Round k:` is not counted when counting words in the chant sentence. The text after each label is one sentence whose word count sequence is exactly 17, 9, 5, 3, 2, 1, 1. For each i from 0 to 5, the sentence in Round i+1 is obtained by deleting exactly the last floor(n/2) words from the sentence in Round i, with no other edits, so the next sentence is word-for-word identical to the remaining prefix. The unique one-word fixed-point sentence in Round 5 is the first word of every chant sentence in Rounds 0 through 5, and that word appears nowhere else in Rounds 0 through 5. Round 6 is word-for-word identical to Round 5, so applying the rule to the one-word sentence deletes 0 words and leaves it unchanged.
  WRITER PROCEDURE (mandatory): first draft round 0 and COUNT ITS WORDS ONE BY ONE, numbering each word (1..n); adjust until the count is exactly the declared n. Then produce each later round by deleting exactly floor(k/2) words from the end of the previous round -- copy the surviving prefix verbatim, never paraphrase. Verify every round's count before output: n, then n-floor(n/2), and so on down to 1, then the 1-word round repeated once.
verify_steps: Check that the opening rule sentence is exactly the quoted sentence, and that the 7 labels are exactly `Round 0:` through `Round 6:` on separate lines; when counting words, ignore the label `Round k:`.
Count the words in the sentence after each label and confirm the sequence is exactly 17, 9, 5, 3, 2, 1, 1.
For each i from 0 to 5, delete the last floor(n/2) words from Round i, where n is the word count of Round i, and compare the result word-for-word with Round i+1.

Extract the single word in Round 5 and Round 6, confirm they are identical, confirm that the same word is the first word of Rounds 0 through 5, and confirm that in Rounds 0 through 5 it appears nowhere except in first position.
contraction_fixed_point.distinguish: It differs from self_reference because the fixed-point word is not justified by semantic self-talk, from convergence because there is only one self-iterating chain, from spiral because the chain only shrinks, from cycle because no earlier complete multiword round reappears, from zeno_halving because the check is exact fixedness after deletion rather than a summed-length claim, from negative_feedback because there is no preannounced target or alternating overshoot, and from recursion because there are no paired entry-and-exit levels.

aperiodic_tiling.device_en:
Device: Aperiodic Tiling as a 21-sentence Fibonacci-beat story. The story has exactly 21 sentences. A word is a maximal run of letters, digits, apostrophes, or hyphens; punctuation outside such runs does not count. Label sentence i as A if it contains no double-quote characters and has at least 15 words; label sentence i as B if it contains exactly one matched pair of double quotes and has at most 8 words. Every one of the 21 sentences must satisfy exactly one of these two labels, and reading the labels in sentence order must give exactly `ABAABABAABAABABAABABA`. Equivalently, let W1 = A, and for n = 1,2,3,4,5,6 let W(n+1) be obtained from Wn by replacing every A with AB and every B with A; the 21-label string must equal W7. That string therefore has exactly 13 A labels and exactly 8 B labels, and 13 and 8 are consecutive Fibonacci numbers with ratio 13/8. For each p in {1,3,7}, the full 21-label string must not equal its first p labels repeated 21/p times. For every length L from 1 through 21, any two contiguous length-L windows in the 21-label string must have A counts that differ by at most 1.
  WRITER PROCEDURE (mandatory): write the 21-slot template letter string first (ABAABABAABAABABAABABA), then compose sentence k to match slot k's letter, one at a time, checking the A/B criterion for that sentence before moving on; finally recheck all 21 in order.
verify_steps: Split the story into exactly 21 sentences, count words by the stated rule, and label each sentence A or B using only the two explicit label tests; then read off the 21-label string in order.

Recompute W7 from W1 = A using the substitution rules A -> AB and B -> A for six successive iterations, compare it to `ABAABABAABAABABAABABA`, and confirm that the string contains exactly 13 A labels and 8 B labels.
For p = 1, 3, and 7, compare the full 21-label string with its first p labels repeated 21/p times and confirm inequality in each case.
Enumerate every pair of contiguous equal-length windows for lengths 1 through 21 and verify that the A-counts in the two windows differ by at most 1 in every comparison.
aperiodic_tiling.distinguish: It differs from tiling and alternation because the 21-label string is not a repetition with period 1 or 2; from interference because the only periodicity test is failure for p in {1,3,7}, not two periods with an lcm; from symmetry_breaking because there is no single violated site in an otherwise periodic background; from recursion because there are no paired entry/exit markers or nested levels; from spiral because 13:8 is only the A:B beat ratio, not level-by-level growth; and from transformed_canon because no fixed-interval verbatim recurrence is required.
